messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher queue growth detected on us-west-2-runtime. error rate spike and multiple container restarts. auto-escalation to #eng-oncall :rotating_light:
ashley_oncall: seeing huge latencies for a subset of customers (p95 -> 12s). dashboards show queue depth ramping on batcher pods, memory climb then OOM and kube restarts. paging activity spiking on node GPUs.
kai_runtime: digging in — looks like the continuous batcher isn't trimming inflight batches when a consumer times out. suspect deadlock causing backlog growth. collecting logs.
ashley_oncall: @kai_runtime can you confirm customer impact list? CS says 2 customers complaining about production latency spikes and one 5xx.
cs_lead: customers A and B reported degraded inference timeouts. customer C saw a single 500 around the same window. All are on hosted API in us-west-2.
kai_runtime: got a tail of the pod logs, pasting snippets:
```
2026-03-15T14:05:32Z batcher: enqueue batch id=0x7f3e size=1024
2026-03-15T14:05:33Z batcher: wait_for_consumers timeout id=0x7f3e
2026-03-15T14:05:33Z batcher: deadlock detected, holding lock: batch_map
2026-03-15T14:05:36Z runtime: cudaMemcpyAsync failed: out of memory (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
2026-03-15T14:05:37Z containerd: task exited with status 137
```
priya_sre: node flapped right after OOMs, kube drained and restarted the pod which caused handoffs to other nodes. paging counters (NV_PAGE_FAULTS) show sustained thrash.
matt_prod: priority = P1 until mitigated. customers A/B are on free-tier burst capacity but still paying in cases, need status for them ASAP.
ashley_oncall: mitigation ideas? temp measures to reduce impact and keep things online.
kai_runtime: immediate mitigations: 1) disable continuous batching flag on service config (fall back to per-request or small fixed batch), 2) scale batcher pool by +2 nodes in us-west-2, 3) temporarily set max_batch_size=256, 4) enable model-variant fallback (lower memory quantized model) for high-latency requests. I'll run commands now.
priya_sre: I'll patch the autoscaler min replicas to prevent flapping during restarts and set eviction thresholds higher for the time being. Also turning on node-level page-allocation throttling.
ashley_oncall: @dev-tools-bot can you run the rollout with canary? want to avoid rolling everything.
dev-tools-bot: command accepted: `./deploy canary --service=batcher --region=us-west-2 --env=prod --strategy=disable-continuous-batcher` queued. ETA 45s.
kai_runtime: applied feature flag override: `continuous_batching=false` on 3 pods. Observability: queue depth down 40% within 90s, latency p95 dropping.
priya_sre: scaled +2 nodes, increased max_batch_size to 256, applied eviction configs. NV_PAGE_FAULTS trending down. No further OOMs in the last 4 mins.
matt_prod: good. notify customers with ETA and root-cause summary.
cs_lead: sending proactive messages to customers A/B/C with interim mitigation note.
ashley_oncall: collecting logs and will open an incident postmortem. tagging as incident-1987654322. Please add any reproductions.
kai_runtime: reproduction notes: stress test with mixed sequence lengths and client timeouts triggers deadlock when batcher misses consumer heartbeat. Adding a fix: ensure consumer heartbeats drop waiting batches and add backpressure window.
priya_sre: will coordinate host-level paging investigation with infra. raising a follow-up to check kernel/pagemap settings and GPU driver version.
matt_prod: next steps: short-term mitigations stayed, rolling canary completed with no further OOMs. Long-term: patch batcher deadlock, add watchdog that kills stale batches, and add automatic fallback to quantized variants under memory pressure.
ashley_oncall: handing this to second shift @jonathan_oncall at 22:00 UTC. summary to include: timeline, customers impacted, mitigations executed, logs attached, follow-ups (pager duty: batcher deadlock patch, infra: GPU paging config).
jonathan_oncall: acked, will monitor and follow up in AM. ping me if it reoccurs.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> service restored to normal in us-west-2. incident severity downgraded to SEV-2. postmortem created: /incidents/1987654322-batcher-handback-oom-cuda-paging.
